info.title: Understudy API
info.description: Part-learning tool for musical theatre vocal scores.

get.description:
Liveness: is the process up. Deliberately touches nothing else, so a database
blip does not cause the orchestrator to kill healthy pods.
Readiness: can we actually serve traffic.

Everything this user owns or has been shared. One query, not N+1: the share role
comes back in the same row via an outer join.

post.description:
Upload a PDF and kick off recognition.

202, not 201: the score exists but is not usable yet. The client gets a job handle
and polls `/jobs/{id}`. Returning 201 with an empty score would be a lie the
frontend then has to special-case.

get.description:
The renderable document. `?versionId=` lets an editor preview a version before
activating it; without it you get whatever is current.

post.description: Re-run recognition on a corrected PDF. Produces a new version; does not activate it.

get.description: Dry run: what would activating this version do to everyone's saved work.

Poll a job.

Polling rather than websockets: an OMR run is minutes long and a handful of clients
watch it, so a 1-3s poll costs a trivial amount and removes a whole class of
connection-lifecycle bugs. Supabase Realtime is the upgrade path if a score ever
needs many simultaneous watchers.
Your own profiles, plus any the score's collaborators have published.

patch.description:
Add/remove notes incrementally.

Chosen over PUT-the-whole-set because selection is a click-by-click gesture: a
diff keeps the request tiny, and two people (or two tabs) editing different parts
of the same profile merge instead of overwriting each other. Adds are idempotent —
re-sending an add the client already made is a no-op, so retries are safe.

put.description:
Idempotent upsert keyed on (author, target, kind).

One annotation of a given kind per target per author: re-colouring a note replaces
its colour rather than stacking a second one. Batched because colouring a whole
voice part is one gesture that touches hundreds of notes, and 300 POSTs would be
300 round trips.

post.description:
Share by email address.

The invitee must already exist in our `users` mirror, i.e. they have signed in at
least once. Inviting a stranger needs an email side channel and a pending-invite
table; for a cast of ten who all sign in on day one, that is not yet worth building.

MigrationReport.title: MigrationReport
MigrationReport.description:
What activating a new score version did to existing user work.

Surfaced to the user rather than silently applied: "14 of your 312 notes no longer
exist in the corrected score" is information a singer needs before a rehearsal.

Note.title: Note
Note.description:
One notated event. Rests carry ``midi=None``.

``onset``/``onset_in_measure``/``duration`` are in ticks; ``ScoreDoc.divisions``
says how many ticks are in a quarter note. Integer ticks rather than seconds so the
document is tempo-independent — changing playback tempo must not rewrite the score.

Part.title: Part
Part.description: A voice part / staff line as OMR understood it: "Elphaba", "Soprano", "Piano R.H.".

ProfileNotesPatch.title: ProfileNotesPatch
ProfileNotesPatch.description:
Incremental edit. Clicking a note sends one add or one remove, not the whole set —
which keeps a 900-note part's edits at a few hundred bytes and makes concurrent
edits by two people commute instead of clobbering.

ScoreDoc.title: ScoreDoc
ScoreDoc.description: Everything the client needs to render and play a score version.

ScoreDocResponse.title: ScoreDocResponse
ScoreDocResponse.description:
The renderable payload: the document plus signed URLs for its page images.

URLs are minted per request and expire, so the response is deliberately
uncacheable while the document itself (the expensive part) is content-addressed
by version ID and cached hard on the client.
